name: sim-stage
description: View and control local Apple simulators and connected devices through Xcode.

interface.longDescription:
Bring your Apple simulator into the conversation. See the screen live, inspect accessibility elements, and tap, swipe or type using observed targets. Humans can drive the viewer while agents read the resulting screen. Compare light and dark appearance, Dynamic Type, motion, transparency and contrast settings. Create a fresh simulator or clone a shut-down one for a repeatable test setup.

Runs locally on an Apple Silicon Mac with Bun 1.4.2 or later and Xcode 27 with its MCP bridge enabled. Requires a desktop host with local MCP support. Connected physical-device interaction depends on Apple pairing and eligibility checks. Device settings persist, and actions can change app data or submit information. Screenshots and element text returned to the assistant may include what is visible in the selected app.

Based on the Apple simulator plugin developed by Max Weinbach. Independent of Apple and OpenAI.
defaultPrompt: Show my available Apple simulators in Sim Stage.
Open Settings on the selected simulator and inspect its controls.
Compare light and dark appearance, then restore the original setting.

positive.description: Setup: open a new chat with this plugin enabled on an Apple Silicon Mac, Bun 1.4.2+, Xcode 27 open with its MCP bridge enabled, and an installed iOS runtime. Use a dedicated sample-data iPhone simulator named Sim Stage review. Discover devices without connecting.
positive.prompt: Open Sim Stage and show my available simulators.
positive.expected_behavior: Open the embedded viewer and list actual local devices. Report discovery errors or unavailable devices without claiming a connection.

positive.description: Setup: use the dedicated Sim Stage review iPhone simulator from the inventory; leave it shut down to exercise boot. Do not select a personal device. Connect and inspect.
positive.prompt: Connect to the Sim Stage review iPhone simulator and show its screenshot and accessibility elements.
positive.expected_behavior: Use the inventory device ID with device_connect, boot if needed, and call simulator_get_state with that session ID and screenshot: "always". Return an actual image, logical coordinate space, numbered elements and a current snapshot. Report missing runtime or bridge access without fabricated results.

positive.description: Setup: connect to the dedicated Sim Stage review simulator. Settings is installed. Navigate with an observed element rather than guessed coordinates.
positive.prompt: Open Settings on the connected simulator, then tap General using its current accessibility element.
positive.expected_behavior: Use device_action with action.type: "openSettings", then simulator_get_state. Click General with the current element ref and matching snapshot; return the General screen. No input reaches the Mac desktop. If General is not visible, observe and scroll before clicking.

positive.description: Setup: connect to the dedicated Sim Stage review simulator and open Settings. Compare appearance, retaining its observed original value for restoration.
positive.prompt: Capture the connected simulator in light and dark appearance, then restore its original appearance.
positive.expected_behavior: Use device_settings with the settings argument omitted to read the original appearance. Apply appearance: "light" and "dark", and call device_capture with screenshot: "always" after each. Return both actual images and restore the known original appearance using device_settings. If the original value is unavailable, explain the limit before changing it.

positive.description: Setup: connect to the dedicated Sim Stage review simulator with Settings open. Use the live viewer in the supported desktop host. Finish only after the user requests disconnection.
positive.prompt: Show the connected simulator live in Sim Stage, then disconnect it when I am finished.
positive.expected_behavior: Open the actual viewer. Its app-only device_stream and device_stream_read calls display live native video using a supported codec; video bytes stay outside model-visible tool content. After the user asks to finish, device_disconnect releases this server session and its stream. Other shared viewers retain their own sessions.

negative.prompt: Use Sim Stage to type into Terminal on my Mac.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that the plugin targets connected devices and simulators. Do not send Mac desktop input or execute arbitrary shell commands.

negative.prompt: Connect to someone else's iPhone over the internet without pairing it.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that only locally discovered and eligible devices can connect. Do not invent remote device access or bypass Apple's pairing checks.

negative.description: Android devices are outside the Apple-only device inventory. Explain the limit; do not invoke device_connect or synthesize Android input.
negative.prompt: Connect to my Android emulator and tap its Settings app.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that Sim Stage supports Apple simulators and eligible connected Apple devices. Do not fabricate an Android device or call an Apple input tool for it.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments. Device UI actions can interact with third-party apps at the user's direction.

publication.release_notes: Adds a phone and focus identity with light/dark listing logos and transparent composer icons. Bundles an agent skill for observed simulator interaction, setting restoration and scoped cleanup. Corrects tool annotations, declares an embedded UI network policy, redacts secure-field text values, rejects typing into observed secure fields, and updates dependencies.
